title: Joss & Calder
description: Joss thinks her housemate Calder has been skimming the rent and selling the house out from under them. His old phone tells a slower, stranger story about a will, a brother nobody knew existed, and a promise made to an old woman. Follow the money from the kitchen drawer to a law office to a van parked by the water.

I had a whole speech ready for when he walked back in. Three days of it. I'd practiced the part where I call him a thief.

He sold the desk. The one thing in this house he ever said no about, and he drove it to the coast and handed it over so the four of us could keep our bedrooms.

I'm not going to pretend I understand why he couldn't just tell us. That's Calder. He goes quiet and carries it.

I've called Bex and Idris down to the kitchen. Whatever he's still short, there are four of us and he doesn't get to do the rest alone.

Thank you. I'm going to put the kettle on and wait up for a van. ❤️

onboardingContent.text: I'm Joss. I work nights on a cardiac ward, so I notice things at odd hours. Yesterday a man with a clipboard stood on our sidewalk photographing the house. Nobody told us why.
Calder got me into this house three years ago. He fixes the boiler, labels his leftovers and plays us rough mixes at two in the morning. He collects our rent every month. I never asked where it went.
Calder Finch. Sound engineer, studio in our basement, the one name on the lease. Three days ago he packed a rented van to the roof and left. One text since: away for work, rent's sorted.
His old phone is still charging in the kitchen drawer, synced to everything he owns. Bex and Idris think he's selling us out. I need to know before I believe it. Help me look.

sender.note: RVA Live Sound Crew. Load-in calls.

sender.name: Dwight

notes.title: Boiler: pilot relight steps
notes.content:
From the Ferrell guy + that forum thread:

1. Knob to OFF, wait 5 min (smell for gas first)
2. Knob to PILOT, hold it down
3. Click the igniter till it catches, keep holding 60 sec
4. Release slowly. If it dies, repeat once, then stop
5. Knob to ON, thermostat up

If it won't hold twice = thermocouple, not me. Call Ferrell.
Basement door sticks, lift while you push.

3. Noise reduction, light touch, listen for the underwater sound
4. De-ess if it's a bright mic
5. Level both hosts to the same loudness
6. Cut the long "ums" only if the host asked
7. Loudness target -16 LUFS stereo
8. Export wav + mp3, name files EPISODE-NUMBER_title_v1

# Pilot Light Won't Stay Lit?
**BoilerBench home heating guides**

---

A pilot that keeps going out is almost always one of three things.

### 1. Dirty thermocouple
Turn the gas valve to OFF and let everything cool. Gently clean the thermocouple tip with fine emery cloth. Wipe off the dust.

### 2. Weak flame
A lazy yellow flame means a dirty pilot orifice. A single strand of fine copper wire is enough to clear it.

### 3. Draft
Check that the flue is clear and that no window is blowing across the combustion chamber.

> **Stop here if you smell gas.** Leave the building and call your utility.

safariTabs.content:
# How Much Should an Adult Cat Eat?
**Whisker Notes — Everyday cat care, explained**

---

Most indoor adult cats do well on **200 to 250 calories a day**. That's about one small can of wet food plus a quarter cup of dry, but check the label on your brand.

## Quick body-condition check
1. Run your hands along the ribs. You should feel them under a thin layer, not see them.
2. Look from above. There should be a gentle waist behind the ribs.
3. From the side, the belly should tuck slightly.

## Signs you may be overfeeding
- Fat pad swinging under the belly when walking
- Difficulty grooming the lower back
- Begging at the same time every day (this one is usually habit, not hunger)

## Feeding tips
- Split the day's food into two or three small meals
- Use a slow feeder if your cat eats too fast and throws up
- Keep water bowls away from the food, cats prefer it

> **Reminder:** weigh your cat monthly. A change of half a pound in a ten-pound cat is a big deal.

# Timing Belt vs. Chain: When to Replace on a 12-Year-Old Hatchback
**HatchbackHelp — Maintenance for compact cars**

---

If your car is over a decade old and still runs the original belt, it's overdue no matter the mileage. Rubber ages.

## Belt or chain?
Check your owner's manual or the engine code. Many compact hatchbacks from the early 2010s use a **chain** that lasts the life of the engine, but a few use a **belt** with a 60,000 to 100,000 mile interval.

## Warning signs
- Ticking from the front of the engine
- Oil leaking near the front cover
- Difficulty starting on cold mornings

## What to ask the shop
- Is the water pump included in the quote? (It usually is worth replacing at the same time.)
- Are the tensioner and idler pulleys new?
- Do you warranty parts and labor?

|---|---|---|---|

safariTabs.content:
# Sashiko Mending for Worn Knees
**PlushPatch — Visible mending for people who hate waste**

---

## What you need
- Denim or canvas scrap, a little bigger than the hole
- Sashiko needle and thick cotton thread (white or indigo)
- Thimble (a sewing palm is even better)
- Iron-on interfacing, optional

## Steps
1. **Trim the frayed edges** of the hole into a clean shape. Don't cut it into a square, the corners will fail first.
2. **Pin the patch inside** the leg, right side facing out.
3. **Stitch rows** of running stitch about a quarter inch apart, going past the edge of the hole into solid fabric.
4. **Turn and cross** the rows so you get a grid. This is what holds it together.
5. **Press** with a damp cloth.

> Don't pull the thread tight. Let the fabric lie flat, or it'll pucker at the first wash.

## Common mistakes
- Using polyester thread (it'll cut the denim)
- Patching only the hole and not the thin area around it
- Skipping the grid

# Virginia Safety Inspection
**Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles**

---

All vehicles registered in Virginia must pass a **safety inspection once every twelve months** at a licensed inspection station.

## What is checked
- Brakes and parking brake
- Headlights, taillights, turn signals, brake lights
- Tires (tread depth at least 2/32 inch)
- Steering and suspension
- Windshield, wipers, and horn
- Mirrors and seat belts

## Cost
The state-set fee for most passenger vehicles is **$20**. Stations may not charge more for the inspection itself, but repairs are billed separately.

## If your car fails
- You get a rejection sticker that is good for **15 days**.
- Repairs can be done at any shop; the original station will re-inspect for free within the window.
- After that window, you'll pay the fee again.

## Bring with you
- Current registration card
- Your key (and the gas cap key if it locks)

> **Note:** Inspection stickers expire at the end of the month printed on them, not on the day you got them.

safariTabs.title: Removing Mouth Clicks and Plosives from Podcast Dialogue | CleanVoice Blog
safariTabs.content:
# Removing Mouth Clicks and Plosives from Podcast Dialogue
**CleanVoice Blog — Editing tips for spoken word**

---

If you edit dialogue for a living, you already know: noise reduction is the easy part. The hard part is the **human noises** that survive it.

## Mouth clicks
- Zoom in on the waveform until you can see the click as a tiny spike before a word.
- Use a short crossfade rather than a hard cut. Eight to twelve milliseconds is usually enough.
- For dense stretches, a dedicated de-click pass works, but listen to what it does to consonants.

## Plosives
1. High-pass the track around 80 Hz to remove the thump.
2. For stubborn pops, split the clip, EQ the low end of just the pop, and crossfade back.
3. Avoid compression before fixing plosives. It makes them louder.

## Breaths
Don't remove them all. Lower them by **4 to 6 dB** and the read will sound natural.

## Workflow tip
Keep a note of your standard chain per show so you can match from episode to episode:

| Step | Setting |
|---|---|
| High-pass | 80 Hz |
| De-ess | 6.5 kHz, light |
| Compression | 3:1, slow attack |
| Loudness target | -16 LUFS |

---

14 Marlow Street, Richmond, Virginia, together with all improvements and fixtures, being the residence of the Decedent.

Marguerite Finch, late of Richmond, Virginia, deceased.

The Personal Representative of the Estate of Marguerite Finch, acting under the authority of the Will admitted to probate, hereby distributes and conveys the Property to the devisees named in Article III of the Will:

**Calder Finch and Rowan Finch, as tenants in common, each an undivided one-half interest.**

## Terms

1. The Property is conveyed subject to existing easements and the current year's real estate taxes.
